papers.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
papers.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated 200-complex dataset (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed Ab-FoldBench subset. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, it compares docking accuracy and interaction specificity across models. The work provides a standardized evaluation framework for choosing co-folding tools in epitope mapping, candidate triage, and antibody engineering.

papers.title: Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
papers.abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A, SKIL, IFNG, and B4GALT1. In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecul
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to the endocrine-disrupting chemical 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1 immune regulation. Using human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling, the authors identified IFNG and SKIL as down-regulated and CDKN1A as up-regulated in allergic rhinitis, with IFNG primarily expressed in T-cells. These findings suggest a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and immune dysregulation in allergic disease.

papers.title: Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.
papers.abstract: Urolithins are polyphenolic compounds produced by gut microbiota from dietary ellagitannins and ellagic acid, with urolithin A being the most bioactive and associated with a range of pharmaceutical activities like anti-aging and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite these benefits, the number of known urolithin A-producing bacteria and their corresponding enzymes is very limited. In this study, we combined conventional sequence-based homology search with structural modeling to identify novel bacteria potentially harboring 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases, primarily characterized in the Enterocloster
papers.summary: The authors combined sequence-based homology searches with structural modeling to identify bacterial candidates for 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase, an enzyme that converts urolithin precursors into the bioactive urolithin A. By analyzing binding pocket conservation across phylogenetically diverse bacteria, they expanded the set of potential urolithin A-producing organisms beyond the few previously known. This work provides new leads for understanding and engineering gut microbial production of a health-relevant polyphenol.

papers.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba
papers.summary: This paper shows that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about multiple protein conformations, even when the model outputs a single structure from a deep multiple sequence alignment. By analyzing these distributions, the authors demonstrate that alternative conformational states can be predicted from a standard AF2 run, offering a route to multi-state structural modeling without extensive MSA manipulation.

papers.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s
papers.summary: The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with sequence-based modeling to engineer enzymes that can use biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors such as NMNH instead of the costly natural cofactor NADPH. This addresses the poor activity of natural enzymes with alternative cofactors, offering a cheaper route for biocatalytic synthesis. The platform aims to overcome limitations of directed evolution and rational design by reducing experimental uncertainty and computational complexity.

papers.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
papers.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en
papers.summary: This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) have produced many predicted binders that fail to translate into clinical candidates. It surveys current computational strategies, catalogs common pitfalls such as poor treatment of metal coordination and conformational flexibility, and proposes ways to improve the translational reliability of in silico inhibitor discovery.

papers.title: In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major public health threat in Africa and South America. Although the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective, its use is restricted in certain vulnerable populations, emphasizing the need for nonreplicating alternatives. We performed an integrated in silico characterization of two production-optimized recombinant YFV envelope (Env) proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains. Physicochemical, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), electrostatic, and immune sim
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) methods to characterize two recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains, which were previously optimized for production. The authors assess physicochemical properties, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, and perform structural modeling, docking, molecular dynamics, and immune simulation. The work supports the development of nonreplicating recombinant subunit vaccine candidates as alternatives to the live-attenuated 17D vaccine, which is restricted in some vulnerable populations.

papers.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.
papers.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how the organic semiconductor NDI-C6 transitions between its two stable crystal polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at higher temperatures). The simulations reproduce both phases' stability and refine unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally, showing the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving both fast and slow molecular motions.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.
papers.abstract: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations generate potential of mean force (PMF) curves that integrate the energy of molecular interactions along a defined pathway, offering a means to understand how PFAS interact with and pass throu
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) curves that describe how diverse PFAS molecules partition into phospholipid bilayers. By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to predict steady-state partition ratios relevant to cellular health. The work addresses the challenge of predicting membrane partitioning across the large chemical diversity of PFAS.

papers.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing
papers.summary: The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins and to gain new insights into the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms. The work demonstrates how structure-based annotation can complement sequence-based methods for organisms with minimal genomes and many proteins of unknown function.

papers.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.
papers.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment-protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pig
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: This study investigates how two structurally similar pigment-protein subunits of Photosystem II, CP29 and LHCII, achieve distinct functional roles in light harvesting despite their structural similarity. By combining 2D electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling, the authors assign spectral features to specific exciton states and show how subtle structural differences tune energy transfer specialization. The work provides molecular-level insight into how protein structure fine-tunes photosynthetic energy transfer networks.

papers.title: Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.
papers.abstract: PFAS coatings impart strong water and oil repellency on materials, but their environmental persistence necessitates sustainable alternatives. The development of alternative chemistries is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic water and oil wettability. Here, a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulation framework was developed to predict and rationalize the intrinsic water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon for both water and oil. By systematically sampling PFAS head group types (-CHO, -COOH,
papers.summary: This paper develops a machine learning framework combined with molecular dynamics simulations to predict how PFAS coatings on nylon repel water and oil, using iterative error-driven refinement to improve predictions. The approach systematically samples different PFAS head group chemistries to understand how molecular structure governs surface wettability, aiming to guide the design of sustainable alternatives to persistent PFAS coatings.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.
papers.abstract: Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. This review treats the electrode-charging methods availablefixed and constant-charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aw
papers.summary: This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for modeling graphene and graphene-derived electrodes paired with ionic liquid electrolytes in supercapacitors. It compares electrode-charging approaches such as fixed/constant-charge, constant-potential, and electronic-structure-aware schemes, and discusses how molecular-scale interfacial structure governs macroscopic capacitance. The work serves as a methods-oriented reference for computational electrochemistry of well-defined carbon interfaces.

papers.title: Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.
papers.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling "photonic substituent effects." Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. Using cavity-constrained QED-DFT geometry relaxations followed by QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations of the Wheland intermediates, we confirm substantial energetic reordering and p
papers.summary: This study uses correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics to revisit a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. By combining QED-DFT geometry relaxations with QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations on Wheland intermediates, the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering and altered selectivity, supporting the concept of a 'photonic substituent effect' on ground-state reactivity.

papers.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.
papers.summary: This study identifies novel small-molecule binders that target different conformational states of the IL-6 receptor (IL-6R) to modulate IL-6 signaling, addressing the challenge of disrupting the large protein–protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R. The work offers a potential route toward orally available alternatives to monoclonal antibody therapies for inflammation and immune-related diseases.

papers.title: The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.
papers.abstract: We assess the sensitivity of time-resolved observables for characterising ultrafast nonadiabatic reaction dynamics. Using the ultrafast (<100 fs) photoisomerisation of norbornadiene as a testbed, we compare the observables for trajectory surface hopping simulations carried out at four different levels of electronic structure theory, SA-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 with (2,2) and (4,4) active spaces, resulting in four different sets of dynamics with distinct lifetimes and branching ratios. For each simulation, we calculate time-resolved photoelectron spectra, and electron- and X-ray scattering signals
papers.summary: This study evaluates how well different time-resolved spectroscopy and scattering techniques can distinguish between competing computational models of an ultrafast photochemical reaction. Using norbornadiene photoisomerization as a test case, the authors simulate dynamics at four levels of electronic structure theory and compute the resulting photoelectron spectra and electron/X-ray scattering signals. The work reveals which observables are most sensitive to underlying nonadiabatic dynamics and can help guide future experiments.

papers.title: Integrating Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Data with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Protein Complex Structure Prediction.
papers.abstract: Ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) provides valuable structural information about protein shape and size through collision cross section (CCS). However, it lacks atomic level structural detail. While AlphaFold has been successful in predicting monomeric protein structure, it can struggle with modeling protein complexes. To address these limitations, we developed a method that integrates IM-MS data with AlphaFold and Rosetta to improve complex structure prediction. Our approach docks AlphaFold predicted subunits with Rosetta and selects the resulting models with a newly developed score that
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that combines ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) collision cross section data with AlphaFold-predicted subunit structures and Rosetta docking to improve protein complex structure prediction. A new scoring function selects the best models by incorporating the experimental IM-MS data, addressing AlphaFold's limitations in modeling complexes.

papers.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.
papers.summary: This study identifies the bisphenol analog bisphenol PH as a high-risk endocrine disruptor that impairs ovarian function by disrupting and downregulating the LHCGR gene. The authors also propose a prioritization framework for ranking endocrine-disrupting chemicals by their reproductive toxicity risk.

papers.title: LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS): A Standardized Representation Language for Lipid Membrane Systems.
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations of lipid membranes lack a standardized, machine-readable representation, creating significant barriers to reproducibility, data sharing, and AI-driven analyses. Current membrane descriptions are fragmented across software-specific input files, making it difficult to reconstruct published systems or compare results among studies. Here, we introduce LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS), a line notation not a simulation tool or membrane-building program, for lipid membrane simulations that extend SMILES, BigSMILES, and CG-BigSMILES to membrane systems. LiMBS version 1.0 uses
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: The authors introduce LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS), a standardized line notation for representing lipid membrane systems used in molecular dynamics simulations. It extends existing chemical notation standards (SMILES, BigSMILES, CG-BigSMILES) to capture membrane composition and organization, addressing the current lack of machine-readable, reproducible descriptions. This enables data sharing, system reconstruction, and AI-driven analyses of membrane simulations.

papers.title: Orf virus early genes ORFV113 and ORFV114 are individually dispensable for replication in vitro but required for full virulence in vivo.
papers.abstract: Orf is a highly contagious zoonotic disease caused by Orf virus (ORFV), resulting in significant economic losses to the livestock industry. ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the terminal variable region of the ORFV genome, are putative virulence-associated genes. To elucidate their biological functions, we characterized the transcription kinetics of both genes and generated single-gene deletion mutants by homologous recombination, using transfer plasmids carrying flanking homology arms and an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) reporter cassette. Lamb testis (LT) cells transfected with the
papers.summary: This study characterizes two putative virulence genes, ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the variable terminal region of the Orf virus genome, and generates single-gene deletion mutants using homologous recombination. Both genes are individually dispensable for viral replication in cell culture but are required for full virulence in vivo, supporting their role as virulence-associated factors. The work provides functional evidence for these genes and useful mutant tools for studying Orf virus pathogenesis.

papers.title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.
papers.abstract: Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation.
papers.summary: The paper introduces PFM (perturbed flow matching), a generative framework for structure-based drug design that overcomes the closed-form marginal distribution constraint of diffusion models by allowing more flexible forward noising processes. This enables better modeling of the complex, pocket-conditioned molecular distributions required for target-specific 3D molecule generation.

papers.title: Recent Advances in High-Entropy Nanozymes: From Fabrication to Applications.
papers.abstract: Nanozymes are artificial enzymes designed to circumvent the inherent limitations of natural enzymes. They have emerged as a transformative paradigm in biomimetic catalysis. High-entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes) are nanomaterials that consist of high-entropy alloys, oxides, sulfides, and other high‑entropy compounds that exhibit enzyme-like catalytic activity. HEAzymes have recently garnered substantial attention as a next-generation nanozyme. The rapid evolution of this field has been propelled by synergistic advances in nanotechnology, biotechnology, catalysis, and computational modeling, offerin
papers.summary: This review surveys high-entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes), nanomaterials made from high-entropy alloys, oxides, sulfides, and related compounds that mimic natural enzyme catalysis. It covers fabrication strategies and applications, arguing that advances in nanotechnology, biotechnology, catalysis, and computational modeling are driving rapid progress in this next-generation nanozyme field.

papers.title: The evolutionary history of transporters of the plastid outer envelope of Chloroplastida- a structure-sequence comparison.
papers.abstract: Plant metabolism heavily relies on plastids, derived from once free-living organisms. However, how two distinct organisms merged into one remains currently only partially understood. Protein-mediated metabolite exchange across the double-membrane plastid envelope is essential for plant cell function. Here, we investigate the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) involved in these transport processes. The mosaic nature of the nuclear genome and the deep evolutionary distance since plastid acquisition are major challenges. To address them, we combine sequence-based analy
papers.summary: This study investigates the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) that mediate metabolite transport in Chloroplastida, using combined sequence-based analysis and structural comparison. The authors address the challenge of the mosaic nuclear genome and deep evolutionary distance since plastid acquisition to trace how these transporters arose. The work provides insight into the evolutionary integration of the plastid into the host cell.

papers.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences.
papers.summary: GPCRAgent is a multi-agent platform that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to support GPCR-targeted drug discovery. It addresses the limitations of standalone LLMs by integrating structured GPCR domain knowledge, aiming to improve interpretability and systematic characterization of receptor functions and ligand interactions.

papers.title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design.
papers.abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: PharmaDiff is a diffusion-based generative model that creates 3D molecules conditioned on a pharmacophore, using a transformer architecture to incorporate an atom-level pharmacophore representation into the generation process. This enables ligand-based de novo design for targets that lack structural or functional data, by steering generation toward molecules that satisfy key pharmacophoric features.

papers.title: HEIWA: Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Water Attention Affects Force Field Accuracy in Structure-Based Protein Language Model ESM3.
papers.abstract: Protein language models have achieved remarkable success in structure prediction and de novo design. However, their understanding of physical interactions remains limited. For structure-based models, we hypothesize that this limitation stems from the absence of explicit solvent modeling: water mediates hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic burial, and electrostatic interactions that govern protein thermodynamics and kinetics, yet current structure-based models treat proteins as if they exist in a vacuum. Using thermophilic protein classification as a proxy task for force-field awareness, per-residue l
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce HEIWA, a hybrid explicit-implicit water attention mechanism for the structure-based protein language model ESM3, addressing the fact that current models treat proteins as if in a vacuum. Using thermophilic protein classification as a proxy for force-field awareness, they show that incorporating explicit solvent modeling improves the model's physical awareness and accuracy. This suggests that solvent representation matters for structure-based protein language models.

papers.title: Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.
papers.abstract: AI-driven cofolding models have become central tools for predicting protein-ligand complexes, yet it remains unclear whether the resulting structures recover the correct protein conformation or merely place the ligand plausibly within an otherwise mispredicted fold. Here, we benchmark four state-of-the-art cofolding models, AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1, and show that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation. As test systems, we use kinases and Class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), families whos
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four leading AI cofolding models (AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1) on kinase and Class A GPCR protein-ligand complexes. The key finding is that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation—models can place a ligand plausibly even when the protein fold itself is mispredicted. This reveals an important limitation in how cofolding model accuracy is currently assessed and interpreted.

papers.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
papers.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify two existing drugs, ebastine and ceritinib, as inhibitors of FtsZ, a key bacterial cell-division protein, in the cancer-associated bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum. These compounds represent candidate antimicrobials that could specifically target F. nucleatum, which is enriched in colorectal cancer tissues, for potential CRC prevention or treatment.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine synthetic metal cofactors with protein scaffolds to enable reactions not found in nature. It focuses on how noncanonical amino acids, incorporated via genetic code expansion, can bridge natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry, expanding the chemical diversity available for catalysis.

papers.title: Azobenzene-mediated reversible conformational switching in 9,9'-bifluorenylidene-based molecular machines.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo-BF-Azo, a visible-light-driven molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9'-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two photoswitchable tetra-ortho-fluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. By using variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy and UV-vis spectroscopy, together with computational studies, we demonstrate that irradiation at 525 nm induces Azo
papers.summary: The authors designed a molecular machine (Azo-BF-Azo) that combines a flexible 9,9'-bifluorenylidene core with two light-switchable azobenzene units. Using NMR, UV-vis spectroscopy, and computations, they show that 525 nm light triggers azobenzene isomerization that drives reversible conformational switching of the whole molecule. This demonstrates external light control over intrinsic molecular motion in a synthetic system.

papers.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepEST, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts Gene Ontology (GO) terms for bacterial proteins by integrating gene expression, gene location, and predicted protein structure. This approach addresses the large fraction of bacterial proteins that remain functionally uncharacterized, potentially improving annotation and understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms.

papers.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven protein design has moved beyond structure prediction to generative creation of novel enzymes, using the vast uncharacterised microbial sequence space as both a source of raw material and a testing ground. It surveys three stages: mining microbial sequence space, generative design of new biocatalysts, and the organism-agnostic nature of these tools. The key message is that AI is shifting enzyme engineering from being limited by natural enzyme diversity toward designing catalysts that do not exist in nature.

papers.title: BioLiP3: a protein-ligand affinity database integrating curated data with LLM-enabled literature mining.
papers.abstract: Quantitative binding affinities and three-dimensional protein-ligand structures provide complementary information essential for structure-based drug discovery, yet these data remain largely disconnected across existing databases and the biomedical literature. We present BioLiP3, a major extension of BioLiP that expands quantitative affinity coverage 13-fold within its structure-centered framework for biologically relevant interactions. BioLiP3 contains 593 423 affinity records, of which 591 820 are linked to three-dimensional protein-ligand structures: 45 386 experimentally resolved PDB comple
papers.summary: BioLiP3 is a major update to the BioLiP database that links quantitative protein-ligand binding affinities to three-dimensional structures, expanding affinity coverage 13-fold. It contains 593,423 affinity records, with 591,820 linked to PDB structures, and uses LLM-enabled literature mining to extract data from publications. This integration provides a unified resource for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an
papers.summary: Researchers characterized the first meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from an archaeon (Pyrococcus sp., PyrDAPDH), which can use either NADH or NADPH to stereoselectively aminate α-keto acids into D-amino acids. This enzyme is notable because such stable, D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are rare, and it enables high-yield D-amino acid synthesis with ammonium as the amino donor and coenzyme recycling.

papers.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en
papers.summary: Poké is a new computational tool that identifies ligandable pockets on protein surfaces by combining energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score. It works on both static protein structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics trajectories, and is designed to catch cryptic sites that only appear after conformational changes. The authors present it as a fast and reliable alternative for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
papers.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. Mice are used in biomedical research due to their genetic similarities to humans and their utility in evaluating systemic activity and safety of therap
papers.summary: The study characterizes Clonixeril (CXL), previously identified as an inhibitor of human STING signaling, and finds that in the murine system it instead acts as a positive modulator of DMXAA-induced murine STING signaling. This species-specific divergence highlights differences in ligand recognition and activation between mouse and human STING, with implications for using mouse models to evaluate STING-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: DTBNet: multimodal 3D geometric perception with hierarchical attention for robust drug-target interaction and binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) and binding affinity (DTA) constitutes a core challenge in accelerating drug discovery. While existing computational methods have made progress, most models struggle to capture critical physicochemical interactions in 3D space due to reliance on 1D sequences or 2D graph structures, and exhibit limited generalization in cold-start scenarios. This study proposes DTBNet, a unified prediction framework integrating multimodal geometric perception and hierarchical attention. The framework constructs heterogeneous embeddings combining local chemi
papers.summary: DTBNet is a unified deep learning framework that predicts drug-target interactions and binding affinities by integrating multimodal 3D geometric perception with hierarchical attention. Unlike prior models relying on 1D sequences or 2D graphs, it constructs heterogeneous embeddings that capture physicochemical interactions in 3D space, aiming to improve generalization in cold-start scenarios. The work addresses a core drug discovery challenge by better modeling spatial binding determinants.

papers.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).
papers.summary: This study investigates how EGCG, a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) modulate the host immune response to clear intracellular Staphylococcus aureus, a major cause of persistent bacteremia. The authors identify the 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR) as a putative target mediating these immunometabolic effects in liver macrophages. The work suggests that EGCG analogs could enhance intracellular bacterial clearance, offering a potential host-directed therapeutic strategy for SAB.

papers.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
papers.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language
papers.summary: HandShake is a new computational tool that predicts which residues of a protein form the binding interface with a specific partner protein, using only sequence information. It combines the ProstT5 protein language model with cross-chain attention to achieve partner-specific predictions at scale, addressing limitations of prior methods that relied on small datasets or required 3D structures at test time.

papers.title: Targeting TLR2 to Overcome Autophagy-Dependent Chemoresistance in Gastric Cancer: Integrating Molecular Docking, Mechanistic Validation, and Therapeutic Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major barrier to effective treatment of gastric cancer (GC), particularly in advanced disease, where cytotoxic chemotherapy often yields limited and transient responses. The present study provides integrated computational and experimental evidence that targeting TLR2 using repurposed small-molecule inhibitors can overcome autophagy-dependent chemoresistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. A library comprising 1555 FDA-approved drugs was sourced from the DrugBank database, virtual screening was executed, and two compounds, Nilotinib (DB04868) and Lomitapide (DB08827),
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study used virtual screening of 1,555 FDA-approved drugs to identify Nilotinib and Lomitapide as TLR2 inhibitors, then validated experimentally that blocking TLR2 overcomes autophagy-dependent chemoresistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. The work integrates molecular docking with mechanistic and therapeutic evaluation, suggesting drug repurposing as a strategy to sensitize chemoresistant gastric cancer.

papers.title: Void-Assisted Extrinsic Charge Trapping Governs Hole Transport in Organic Semiconductors.
papers.abstract: To realize electrically pumped organic lasing, single-layer devices without organic heterointerfaces have been employed to suppress efficiency rolloff. In such architectures, on the other hand, extrinsic trap states result in trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, thereby decreasing electroluminescence efficiency. Here, we elucidate the dominant factors governing extrinsic trap formation by combining current density (J)-voltage (V) characteristics of single-layer hole-only-devices (HODs) with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 6,6'-bibenzo[d]oxazole (BZ) derivatives exhibiting high phot
papers.summary: This study investigates how extrinsic trap states form in single-layer organic semiconductor devices, which are being explored for electrically pumped organic lasing. By combining current-voltage measurements of hole-only devices with molecular dynamics simulations of BZ derivatives, the authors identify void-assisted extrinsic charge trapping as the dominant factor governing hole transport. This insight could help guide molecular design to reduce trap-assisted nonradiative recombination and improve electroluminescence efficiency.

papers.title: From "undruggable" to tractable: Therapeutic advances targeting Kristen rat sarcoma viral homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C)-mutant cancers and emerging resistance mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This review explains the evolution of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C) from an "undruggable" target to a manageable oncogenic driver in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While first-generation inhibitors have significantly improved patient care, the emergence of complex resistance mechanisms necessitates a shift toward precision-driven combination therapies and advanced computational drug discovery. The KRAS G12C mutation is a primary driver in approximately 8.9% of NSCLC patients, particularly smokers. The development of covalen
papers.summary: This review traces how KRAS G12C, once considered undruggable, became a tractable target in non-small cell lung cancer, where it drives roughly 8.9% of cases, especially in smokers. It covers the first-generation covalent inhibitors that have improved patient outcomes and discusses the complex resistance mechanisms that emerge, arguing for precision combination therapies and computational drug discovery going forward.

papers.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
papers.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map interactions among the many Golgi-associated proteins for which molecular assemblies remain undefined. By extending complex characterization beyond the well-studied subset, the work aims to uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms underlying Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis.

papers.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
papers.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study takes a family-level approach to structural clustering across the tree of life, analyzing 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database to profile their taxonomic composition. The authors identify candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and uncover a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds, expanding the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins beyond what sequence-based methods can detect.

papers.title: Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Computational methods are increasingly applied to the discovery of plant-derived peptides, but the extent, composition and reporting practice of this literature have not been mapped. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed were searched for records published between 2021 and 2026. Of 5062 unique records, 593 were screened at title and abstract, 88 full texts were assessed, 80 sources met all five eligibility criteria and 79 were charted. Overall, 49 (62.0%) were primary studies, 12 (15.2%) described a tool or database and 18 (
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the literature (2021–2026) on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources. It finds that most work consists of primary studies, with a smaller share describing tools or databases, and highlights gaps in reporting practice across the field. The review provides a structured overview of methods, scope, and evidence quality in this emerging area.

papers.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
papers.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r
papers.summary: The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) for interaction with the African swine fever virus ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirmed the predicted I215L–FAM105A interaction, and structural analyses characterized the binding interface. This provides a structure-based workflow for identifying host–viral protein interactions and nominates a new host factor relevant to ASFV replication.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify matrix metalloproteinases MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, then characterizes the structural basis of these interactions. The work suggests a possible mechanistic link between these dietary polyphenols and inhibition of MMP-mediated tumor invasion, though the findings are based on in silico predictions rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and virtual screening to test whether cyclotides—small, stable plant peptides—can bind to CYP19A1 (aromatase), the enzyme that produces estrogen. The authors identify cyclotide scaffolds with predicted affinity for the enzyme, proposing them as starting points for developing modulators of local estrogen production in adenomyosis. The work is entirely in silico, so experimental validation of binding and activity remains to be done.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer under exposure to synthetic phenolic antioxidants: An integrated network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how synthetic phenolic antioxidants (common food additives) might interact with multiple molecular targets involved in colorectal cancer progression. The authors built a library of traditional and novel antioxidants, predicted their toxicity and carcinogenicity, and integrated target predictions from several databases with known CRC-related genes to identify potential mechanisms. The work is entirely computational and does not experimentally validate the predicted interactions.

papers.title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study uses integrated computational and experimental approaches to identify NOS2 (inducible nitric oxide synthase) as a candidate molecular mediator linking air pollutant exposure to depression. The authors combine bioinformatics analysis of pollutant- and depression-associated datasets with experimental validation to propose NOS2 as a mechanistic bridge. The work offers preliminary clues for prevention and treatment but the causal chain remains to be established.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of Coumarin-Triazole Derivatives Targeting the Conserved QGDNQ Motif of Chandipura RdRp.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV) is a recently discovered neurotropic virus associated with severe encephalitis in children and for which there is currently no specific antiviral treatment. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is an attractive antiviral target because of its essential role in viral RNA synthesis and the presence of conserved catalytic motifs required for polymerase function. In this study, a structure-based computational approach was employed to investigate coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors targeting the conserved QGDNQ motif-containing region of CHPV RdRp.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structure-based methods to screen coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of the Chandipura virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, targeting its conserved QGDNQ catalytic motif. The work identifies candidate compounds in silico for a virus that currently lacks any approved antiviral treatment. No experimental validation is described in the abstract, so the findings remain computational predictions.

papers.title: Targeting IL-1R1 and androgen receptor using natural compounds from Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum: an in silico and in vitro study.
papers.abstract: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and in vitro assays to identify natural compounds from two medicinal plants (Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum) that can simultaneously inhibit IL-1R1 (an inflammation receptor) and the androgen receptor (AR), which drive lung and prostate cancers respectively. The dual-targeting approach aims to overcome therapeutic resistance by blocking both inflammatory and hormone-dependent cancer pathways.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
papers.abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study combines network toxicology with experimental validation to identify VCAM1 as a potential molecular mediator linking pyrethroid pesticide exposure to keloid formation. The authors integrate toxicogenomic and disease network data to prioritize candidate genes, then validate VCAM1 as a hub connecting pyrethroid-induced pathways with keloid-associated fibroproliferative processes. The work suggests an environmental exposure–gene interaction that may contribute to keloid pathogenesis.

papers.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.
papers.summary: This study profiles the N-glycoproteome in a mouse model of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), a chronic lung disease of preterm infants marked by arrested alveolarization. The authors identify aberrant N-glycosylation of integrin beta-1 (ITGB1), suggesting a link between glycosylation-dependent ECM-receptor signaling and impaired lung development. The work provides a first N-glycoproteomic landscape for BPD and nominates ITGB1 glycosylation as a candidate pathogenic mechanism.

papers.title: Biocompatible nanoscale contrast agents for MRI and CT scans: current progress and clinical potential.
papers.abstract: Conventional contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) have long served as the backbone of diagnostic imaging. Yet, their well-recognized limitations, including nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and progressive gadolinium deposition with Gd-based chelates, contrast-induced nephropathy with iodinated agents, and serious hypersensitivity reactions with approved iron oxide formulations, continue to drive the search for safer alternatives. Nanoparticle-based contrast agents (NCAs) have emerged as a compelling next generation of imaging tools, offering a degree o
papers.summary: This review surveys nanoparticle-based contrast agents as alternatives to conventional MRI and CT contrast agents, which carry risks such as nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, gadolinium deposition, contrast-induced nephropathy, and hypersensitivity reactions. It covers current progress in biocompatible nanoscale agents and assesses their clinical potential for safer diagnostic imaging.
